subject: Ops readout: AtlasPay latency spike — exec summary & action cadence
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ops readout: AtlasPay latency spike — exec summary & action cadence

Team,

Summary (TL;DR): On 2028-05-17 21:40 UTC we observed a sustained 450–700ms P50 -> P90 latency shift for the AtlasPay tenant affecting hosted API traffic for ~38 minutes. Root cause: a malformed KV-cache invalidation sequence triggered by a regression in a routing change deployed in candidate on 2028-05-17 20:58 UTC. There was graceful degradation to a lower-capacity model variant but some tails impacted customer SLAs. No data exfiltration.

What I ran in the first hour:
- Containment: reverted the routing change (20:58) and forced a cache-warm task to rebuild prefixes.
- Customer mitigation: enabled dedicated routing for AtlasPay leading to improved latency at 22:18 UTC.
- Forensics: captured engine traces and KV-cache logs; created preliminary postmortem.

Attached: postmortem PDF (top-level findings + timeline) and a CSV action tracker with owners.

Immediate executive asks (for QBR prep/OKR check-in):
1) Approve the proposed blitz to harden cache invalidation semantics (2-3 sprints) — estimated +0.6 FTE for SRE/infra in H2.
2) Sign-off on a short-term SLA exception credit proposal for AtlasPay (per Vivek’s prior guidance) and confirm messaging cadence.
3) Agree owners and escalation cadence to surface similar tenant-tail regressions to leadership faster.

Key asks from me in the next 48h:
- Vivek: decision on the credit/compensation approach (outline attached).
- Hannah: confirm triage owners and ETA for the validation harness we discussed.
- Marissa/Laura: prep a 5-min slide for QBR with customer impact and mitigation story (deadline: 2028-05-19 EOD).

Full timeline and technical analysis in attached doc; below are the high-level action items I care about for leadership review.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: atlas-latency-postmortem-20280518.pdf (pdf, 12 pages), action-tracker-atlas-20280518.csv (csv, 1 sheet)

Markus —

Thanks for the crisp summary. I approve the short-term customer credit proposal with the following constraints: cap the credit to one billing cycle for the affected endpoints and prioritize a clear customer message draft before operations outreach. Please route the customer-facing note through Legal quick review; Hannah, loop Legal on the draft.

Continue with the cache-hardening plan; happy to allocate SRE runway if we can show measurable gating tests in Q3.

-v
